subject: biology
title: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells
key_idea: All cells have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and genetic material. Plant and animal cells are **eukaryotic**: their DNA is inside a nucleus. Bacterial cells are **prokaryotic**: they are much smaller, have no nucleus, and their DNA is a single loop, often with extra small rings of DNA called plasmids.

blocks.text: Every living thing is made of cells. Biologists sort cells into two types by where they keep their genetic material. A **eukaryotic cell** keeps its DNA inside a nucleus. Animal cells, plant cells, fungal cells such as yeast, and protists are all eukaryotic.
A **prokaryotic cell** has no nucleus. Its DNA is free in the cytoplasm. Bacteria are prokaryotic cells.

Eukaryotic cells also contain **membrane-bound organelles**. These are sub-cellular structures wrapped in their own membrane, such as the nucleus, mitochondria and chloroplasts. Prokaryotic cells have none of these.
Some structures are found in every cell. Others are found only in one type. The comparison below is the one exam questions ask about most.

blocks.text: Plant cells have three things animal cells do not: a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole. Not every plant cell has chloroplasts. Cells in roots and potatoes get no light, so they do not photosynthesise and have no chloroplasts.
Some bacteria also have a flagellum, a tail-like structure used for movement, and a slime capsule on the outside.

rows: Contains the genetic material (chromosomes) and controls the activities of the cell.
A jelly-like liquid where most of the cell's chemical reactions happen.
Controls which substances enter and leave the cell. It has receptor molecules that let cells communicate.
Where aerobic respiration happens. Respiration releases energy for the cell.
Contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis.
Strengthens and supports the cell. In plants it is made of cellulose.
Filled with cell sap. It helps keep the cell firm.
Carries most of the bacterium's genes.
Small rings of extra DNA carrying a few extra genes, such as genes for antibiotic resistance.

blocks.text: Cells are tiny, so they are measured in small units. From the millimetre down, each unit is 1000 times smaller than the one above it.

So 1 mm = 1000 µm and 1 µm = 1000 nm. To change to a smaller unit, multiply by 1000. To change to a bigger unit, divide by 1000. Sizes this small are often written in **standard form**: 2 µm is 2 × 10⁻⁶ m.

An **order of magnitude** is a factor of ten. To compare two sizes, divide the bigger one by the smaller one. An answer of about 10 means one order of magnitude (10¹). An answer of about 100 means two orders of magnitude (10²).

items.text: An animal cell is 20 µm across. A bacterial cell is 2 µm long.

items.lead: Write as a power of ten

items.text: The animal cell is one order of magnitude bigger than the bacterial cell.

blocks.text: Working out the real size of a cell from a microscope image uses magnification, which has its own note.

checks.q: Give three ways a bacterial cell is different from an animal cell.
checks.a: Any three: it is smaller; it has no nucleus (its DNA is free in the cytoplasm); its DNA is a single loop; it may have plasmids; it has no mitochondria; it has a cell wall; its ribosomes are smaller.

checks.q: Name two structures found in both a plant cell and a bacterial cell.
checks.a: Any two: cell membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, cell wall.

checks.q: A plant cell is 60 µm long. A bacterial cell is 0.6 µm long. How many orders of magnitude bigger is the plant cell?
checks.a: 60 ÷ 0.6 = 100 = 10². The plant cell is two orders of magnitude bigger.

exam_phrases: bacterial cell does not have its DNA inside a nucleus
DNA is free in the cytoplasm
has a single loop of DNA
cell wall in bacterial cells is not made of cellulose

mistakes.wrong: Bacterial cells do not have ribosomes.
mistakes.right: They do. Bacterial ribosomes are smaller than those in plant and animal cells. AQA does not accept the idea that bacteria have no ribosomes.

mistakes.wrong: A eukaryotic cell does not have a cell wall.
mistakes.right: Plant cells and fungal cells are eukaryotic and do have a cell wall, so AQA rejects this. Compare the specific cells named in the question.

mistakes.wrong: A bacterial cell has no chloroplasts, unlike a eukaryotic cell.
mistakes.right: Animal cells have no chloroplasts either, so AQA ignores this when the comparison is with eukaryotic cells in general. Use the nucleus, mitochondria, the single loop of DNA or plasmids.
AQA ignores 'genetic information'. Write DNA or genetic material.

worked_example.question:
Cells are the basic units of all forms of life.

Describe four differences between a bacterial cell and a plant cell.
answer_points: The bacterial cell is smaller than the plant cell.
The bacterial cell does not have its DNA inside a nucleus; the plant cell does.
The bacterial cell may have plasmids; the plant cell does not.
The bacterial cell has no chloroplasts or mitochondria; the plant cell has both.
The bacterial cell wall is not made of cellulose; the plant cell wall is.
The bacterial cell has no large permanent vacuole; the plant cell does.
worked_example.tip: Any four of these score. Make it clear which cell has the feature, or AQA reads 'it' as the bacterium.

exam_phrases: no nucleus / chromosomal DNA (in the cytoplasm)
mitochondria are where respiration occurs / release energy
ribosomes are where proteins are made

mistakes.right: Edexcel ignores 'makes' or 'produces' energy. Write that mitochondria are where respiration happens, which releases energy.

mistakes.wrong: A bacterial cell has a nucleus and mitochondria.
mistakes.right: It has neither. Its DNA is chromosomal DNA free in the cytoplasm. Listing nucleus or mitochondria as a bacterial feature loses the mark.

mistakes.wrong: Plant and animal cells both have a cell wall.
mistakes.right: Only plant cells have a cell wall. The structures in plant cells but not animal cells are the cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

worked_example.question:
Figure 18 shows a bacterial cell and a plant cell.

Describe the similarities and differences of a bacterial cell and a plant cell.
answer_points: Similarities: both cells have a cell membrane, a cell wall, cytoplasm and ribosomes, and both contain DNA.
The bacterial cell has chromosomal DNA free in the cytoplasm; the plant cell has a nucleus containing its DNA.
The bacterial cell has plasmid DNA; the plant cell does not.
The bacterial cell may have flagella for movement; the plant cell does not.
The plant cell has chloroplasts, mitochondria and a vacuole; the bacterial cell has none of these.
The bacterial cell is smaller and is prokaryotic; the plant cell is eukaryotic.
worked_example.tip: This is marked by levels. The top level needs both similarities and differences, written as clear, linked sentences.

exam_phrases: in eukaryotes the DNA is contained in the nucleus
in prokaryotes it is in the cytoplasm
a strand in eukaryotes but a loop in prokaryotes
the ribosome is the site of protein synthesis

mistakes.wrong: Eukaryotic DNA is a double helix but prokaryotic DNA is a loop.
mistakes.right: All DNA is a double helix, so OCR ignores this. Compare the shape: a linear strand in eukaryotic cells and a loop in prokaryotic cells.

mistakes.wrong: Plant cells and bacterial cells are similar because both have DNA.
mistakes.right: OCR ignores DNA as the similarity here. Name a structure both have: cell membrane, cell wall, ribosomes or cytoplasm.

mistakes.wrong: Ticking two boxes in a row of a table to be safe.
mistakes.right: More than one tick in a row scores no mark for that row. Decide, then tick once.

worked_example.question: Compare the DNA found in eukaryotic and in prokaryotic cells.
answer_points: In eukaryotic cells the DNA is contained in the nucleus.
In prokaryotic cells the DNA is in the cytoplasm.
In eukaryotic cells the DNA is in strands, but in prokaryotic cells it is a loop.
Prokaryotic cells have plasmids; eukaryotic cells do not.
In both, the DNA is made of the same parts (nucleotides).
worked_example.tip: Any three. Each point should say something about both types of cell.
